response.description:
Azure
IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029.
You can continue using Azure IoT Central until the retirement date, but we
recommend starting your transition planning early.Why
is this happening?As
Azure IoT evolves, Microsoft is focusing future investment on Azure IoT
platform services that provide greater scalability, architectural flexibility,
lifecycle management, and integration with Microsoft Fabric for analytics and
AI-driven workloads. Azure IoT Hub, Device Provisioning Service (DPS), and
Azure Device Registry represent the recommended Azure-native platform for
connected operations.Recommended
action 
 Review
     your current Azure IoT Central applications, devices, dashboards, ,
     and integrations.
 Evaluate
     Azure IoT Hub and DPS as the target architecture for device connectivity
     and provisioning.
 Evaluate
     Microsoft Fabric for real-time analytics, dashboards, and broader data
     experiences.
 Use the Azure IoT Central
     migration playbook to map existing IoT Central
     scenarios to Azure IoT services. 
 Begin
     planning and executing your transition before September 20, 2029. 
 If
     additional assistance is required, engage Microsoft field teams or an Azure IoT migration partner. Help
and support If
you have questions, get answers from community experts through Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and need technical assistance, create
an Azure support request.
response.title: Retirement: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
